absent: Locking, interrupt safety, and SMP synchronization for debugger globals, environment table, macro list, and history buffers.
Definitions, numeric values, and side effects of keyboard controller registers and status bits, translation tables, and key type helpers.
Full command table, parser, permission model, flag definitions, and helpers for address parsing, symbol lookup, breakpoints, and task CPU queries.
Memory model constants and helpers for page size, page frame validation, word size, allocation flags, and safe area accessors.
Configuration values for default command enablement, catastrophic continuation, grep length, radix defaults, and platform environment additions.
Initialization order, caller contexts, and reboot and CPU relaxation guarantees.

findings.text: Keyboard polling entry for the debugger console checks debugger flags and controller presence, records keyboard existence, reports absence when no output data is ready, otherwise consumes one scan code plus status, discards mouse events and releases except for modifier tracking, updates caps and shift and control state, translates make codes through plain and shifted and control tables, maps navigation and editing keys to control characters, filters unprintables, and returns either one decoded byte or a negative sentinel.

Keyboard modifier state persists across calls. Caps lock toggles on its make code. Shift and left control set on make and clear on break. Other releases are ignored, with one return release clearing a return tracking flag. The combined lock plus shift plus control state selects which translation table applies to the next make code.

Translation maps backspace to a destructive character, enter to carriage return while setting a return seen flag, and tab delete home end plus arrows to control characters. Two layout specific codes are remapped before lookup. Lookup prefers the plain table with no modifier, the shifted table with caps or shift, and the control table with control, then masks the value, normalizes tab, accepts printable letters and selected controls plus enter, and rejects other special or default types.
Module parameter prefix for debugger parameters is a short lowercase name followed by a dot.
Command enablement mask defaults from build configuration and gates sensitive operations such as prompt changes.
Global grep filtering state holds a pattern buffer plus flags for active filtering and leading and trailing context behavior.
Core debugger globals track flags, owning CPU, next line control, general state, current task and register context, fatal message pointer, and go repetition count.
Debugger ownership starts unassigned and line continuation starts enabled.
Catastrophic continue control has two build variants, one initialized from configuration and one zero initialized, both held in a static unsigned value.

Diagnostic message entry pairs a numeric diagnostic code with a pointer to human readable text. A helper defines table entries from a symbolic suffix and text. The static table covers command, argument, width, radix, environment, allocation, breakpoint, address, register, CPU, length, and permission failures.

Environment storage is a fixed pointer array with compiled defaults for prompt selection that differs by multiprocessing support, more prompt, radix, memory display count, platform additions, display table count, and section suppression.

Environment assignment allocates a combined name value entry, replaces an existing entry on exact name match at delimiter boundary while freeing old storage, otherwise occupies the first empty slot, and reports allocation failure or table full conditions.
Environment listing walks the fixed table and prints each non empty entry on its own line.
Unsigned 64 bit argument parser converts a string with automatic base detection and reports a bad integer diagnostic on failure.

Set command accepts compact and spaced assignment forms, normalizes the latter, requires exactly one assignment, denies prompt changes without memory read permission, handles an internal debug flag variable with mask validation and flag merging, and delegates other names to environment assignment.

Macro command object embeds a generic command descriptor plus a list head for ordered statements. Each statement node holds statement text plus a list link. A global pointer holds the macro under construction and a boolean tracks whether definition is in progress.

Define command lists all existing macros with usage and help and statements when invoked without arguments, auto closes a prior unterminated definition on nesting, restricts creation to initialization context, allocates macro and name and usage and help with dequoting for the latter two, initializes the statement list, marks definition in progress, and unwinds allocations with a diagnostic on failure.
String duplication helper strips one pair of surrounding double quotes when present, reserves space for terminator, copies the payload, terminates explicitly, and returns null on allocation failure.

Macro execution requires no extra arguments, locates its own command descriptor by name match, reports not implemented when missing, then sequentially announces and parses each stored statement and stops at the first error.
Command history depth is thirty two entries.
Single command line buffer length is two hundred characters.
Maximum argument count for command parsing is twenty.
Environment pointer table holds thirty one slots.
History management uses head and tail and current indices plus a two dimensional history array and a current line buffer.
Reboot command requests emergency restart and, if control returns, reports the failure and spins indefinitely with CPU relaxation, never returning normally.
Current task selection records the task pointer and resolves register context from per CPU debugger information when the task is associated with a CPU, otherwise clears the register pointer.
Task register accessor resolves per CPU debugger information for a given CPU number.
State diagnostic entry prints a caller supplied label with current CPU, supplied value, initial owning CPU, and global state in hexadecimal.

Memory display supports raw byte dump, plain dump, symbolic dump, physical dump, and width suffixed forms with optional repeat suffix. It loads defaults from environment, reuses persisted address and radix and width and repeat when invoked without arguments, parses address with offset plus optional count and radix, validates radix and width, aligns address down to word boundary, iterates lines with interrupt checks and leading zero detection, suppresses long zero runs with a range message, and persists resume state.

Single display line prints address with physical or virtual prefix, fetches each word through physical or virtual accessors, formats values per caller format, resolves near symbols when symbolic mode is active with optional module and section detail, otherwise accumulates printable equivalents with fallback placeholders using endian aware byte extraction, and pads incomplete lines before showing the character side buffer.

Sized memory accessors accept widths of one two four and eight bytes, zero the output on entry for reads, delegate to area or physical movers, enforce native word size limits for eight byte operations, and report a bad width diagnostic with function prefixed logging for unsupported sizes.

Physical read helper derives page frame from address shift, validates the frame, converts to page structure, creates a temporary local mapping, copies the requested bytes at page offset, unmaps, and reports failure for invalid frames.

Raw dump helper reads consecutive bytes through safe area access, prints each as two hexadecimal digits without separators, terminates with a newline, and stops silently at the first unreadable address.

Memory modify command validates the width suffix, requires address and value arguments, parses both through address argument handling with offset support, enforces exact argument consumption, defaults width to native word size when no suffix is present, writes through the sized writer, and echoes address and written value.
Function prefixed logging helper prepends the enclosing function name to a formatted message.
Area write helper forwards an address and a value to a sized implementation passing the value address and its size.
